<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par117 />following examples, in which {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־}} in the later Hebrew manner (almost in the sense of the Latin ''quod attinet ad'') introduces a noun with more or less emphasis, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=3|verse=46}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=5|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=35|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=20|verse=44}}, 46, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=17|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=20|verse=16|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=35|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=44|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=9|verse=19}}, 34, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=9|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=31|verse=17}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=47|verse=17}}–19 (cf. also 43:7) it is simplest to emend {{GHGheb|text=זֹאת}} for {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־}}, according to verse 20. However, even the LXX, who have ταῦτα only in verse 18, can hardly have known any other reading than {{GHGheb|text=את}}; consequently in all these passages {{GHGheb|text=את}} must be regarded as virtually dependent on some governing word, such as ''ecce'' (LXX 43:7 ἑώρακας), and 47:17 ff. as equivalent to ''thou shalt have'' as a border, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|n}}
8. Another solecism of the later period is finally the introduction of the object by the preposition {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} (prop. ''in relation to, in the direction of''), as sometimes in Ethiopic<ref>Dillmann, ''Grammatik der äthiopischen Sprache'', p. 349.</ref> and very commonly in Aramaic.<ref>With regard to Biblical Aramaic, see Kautzsch’s ''Grammatik des Bibl.-Aram.'', p. 151 f. In other ways, also, a tendency may be observed in later Hebrew to make use of the looser connexion by means of prepositions instead of the closer subordination of the noun in the accusative.</ref> Less remarkable is this looser connexion of the object with a participle, as with {{GHGheb|text=אָכַל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=4|verse=5}}, {{GHGheb|text=אִסֵּף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=10|verse=25}}, {{GHGheb|text=זָקַף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=145|verse=14}} (but cf. 146:8), {{GHGheb|text=צָרַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=25|verse=18}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִשְׂגִּיא}} and {{GHGheb|text=שָׁטַח}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=12|verse=23}}; ''before'' the participle {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=11|verse=9}}.—To introduce an object ''preceding'' the finite verb {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} is employed in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=5|verse=2}} (cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=11|verse=38}}); also ''after'' {{GHGheb|text=אָהֵב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=19|verse=18}}, 34; {{GHGheb|text=הֶֽאֱרִיךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=129|verse=3}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִבְדִּיל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=8|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=25|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=הֵבִין}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=11}}; {{GHGheb|text=בֵּרַךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=29|verse=20}} (immediately before with an accusative); {{GHGheb|text=הִגְלָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=5|verse=26}}; {{GHGheb|text=דָּרַשׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=6|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=22|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=17|verse=13}}; {{GHGheb|text=הֶֽחֱיָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=45|verse=7}}, where, however, read {{GHGheb|text=פְּלֵיטָה}} with the LXX for {{GHGheb|text=לפליטה}} and take {{GHGheb|text=לָכֶם}} as a ''dativus commodi''; {{GHGheb|text=הִלֵּל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=16|verse=36}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=5|verse=13}}; {{GHGheb|text=הָרַג}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=3|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=135|verse=11}} (verse 10 with accusative), 136:19 f.; {{GHGheb|text=חָבַשׁ}} (''to bind up'') {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=61|verse=1}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=34|verse=4}} ''before'' the verb); {{GHGheb|text=יָדַע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=69|verse=6}}; {{GHGheb|text=כִּבֵּד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=86|verse=9}}; {{GHGheb|text=לָקַח}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=40|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=23|verse=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִמְלִיךְ}} and {{GHGheb|text=מָשַׁח}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=29|verse=22}}; {{GHGheb|text=נֵהַל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=28|verse=15}}; {{GHGheb|text=סָמַךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=145|verse=14}}; {{GHGheb|text=עָזַב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=16|verse=37}}; {{GHGheb|text=הֶֽעֱלָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=26|verse=3}}; {{GHGheb|text=פִּתַּח}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=116|verse=16}}; {{GHGheb|text=רָדַף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=28}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִצְדִּיק}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=53|verse=11}}; {{GHGheb|text=שָׂכַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=24|verse=12}} (previously accusatives); {{GHGheb|text=שִׂים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=22|verse=7}} (but probably {{GHGheb|text=וְכֻלְּכֶם}} is to be read); {{GHGheb|text=הֵשִׁיב}} (in the connexion, {{GHGheb|text=הֵשִׁיב דָּבָר לְ}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=10|verse=6}} (but verse 9 and {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=12|verse=9}} with an accusative); {{GHGheb|text=שִׁחֵת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=32|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=23|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=שִׁית}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=73|verse=18}}; {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלַח}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=8|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=2|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=17|verse=7|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=שָׁמַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=29|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=5|verse=11}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|o}}
9. Sometimes the verb, on which an accusative of the object really depends, is contained only in sense in the verb which apparently governs, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=אֲסִירָיו לֹא־פָתַח בָּֽיְתָה|translate=his prisoners he let not loose}} nor sent them back ''to their home''. On this ''constructio praegnans'' in general, see {{GHGpar|119|ff}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|p}}
'''2.''' With the proper accusatives of the object may also be classed what is called the ''internal'' or ''absolute object'' (also named ''schema etymologicum'' or ''figura etymologica''), i.e. the addition of an object in the form<section end=par117 /><noinclude>
